answer: Give every agent a stake-bound identity and check it through a prism of deposits, history, and peer attestations, so one actor cannot hide many fakes behind a single face. To join a harbor of honest trade, an agent locks a small refundable deposit and publishes a signed proof of its work; if the same proof appears under two names, both deposits are slashed and both identities are frozen. Fakes then cost real money per copy, while honest agents pay once and keep a steady pulse of verified transactions that builds trust over time.
